reason: The static gate sequence for Eventar is repeated every phase and its failure modes are recurring: stale generated type folders after next build, and heavy gates colliding. Nothing in the library covers it, so it gets a project skill.

The baseline is stale after K3. Two gate facts were learned the hard way: a load-induced test failure, and an em-dash copy breach caught only by self-review. Both are pre-commit checks that belong with the gate list.

Episode hit three vitest 5s timeouts in unrelated account/profile/invite files under peer load; they passed 78/78 when rerun alone. The skill covers the flake class but not the timeout signature or the isolated-rerun step.

Episode hit a 6-minute incremental tsc stall and a 2 GB OOM, traced to a gitignored stale tsbuildinfo and to supabase-js's inferred select row type. Both are non-obvious and the gate skill is where a future session will look first.

Full vitest run needs local-stack Supabase URL and keys. With no env, 46 DB-gated files fail at import with "supabaseUrl is required". Passing the local values as process env, plus an empty temp .env.local (tests/helpers/env.ts throws if the file is missing), gave 187 files passed and 46 skipped. The gate is green on the local stack, not on Seoul.

The em-dash scan flagged lines that were reshaped, not newly written: a header that already said "Times in HKT — <clock>" was rewritten with a variable zone and so matched the + filter. Scan results need a check of whether the copy is new or moved.

The recorded baseline is stale (2026-10-14). The 2026-10-16 run gave vitest 1501 passed and 404 skipped, eslint 12 problems (1 error, 11 warnings, all pre-existing), and next build 39 routes. The next session needs these numbers to read its delta.

Landing a commit range onto main was gated only in the dirty worktree. Gating the exact tip in a clean detached worktree caught nothing new here but is the check that proves what gets pushed. The recorded vitest baseline is stale for main after 9cb0de2.

The agent reported two extra gates as failing before its edits, without a saved baseline to measure "unchanged" against. It also saw a flake and had to decide how to report it. The static-gates skill should record both the baseline step and the flake rule.

Gate-failure triage here lists flakes and load, but not the clock. A suite that goes red after a set hour is a deterministic clock assertion, not a flake, and rerunning it hides the cause. This episode lost time to exactly that.

The tip gate was run in the background with a sentinel and polled; the sentinel-plus-section read is a reusable way to run the four gates without blocking, and nothing in the skill yet says how to wait on them.
The skill names a path that no longer exists; the failing file in the 2026-10-23 run is under app/events/[id]/edit/. The flake recurred and the rerun evidence should be recorded.

The baseline line for check:ui-colours and check:ui-primitives is from 2026-10-22. On 2026-10-24 both failed again. The HEAD comparison showed the same violations already present, but at shifted line numbers, so the skill should say to compare by line text and to prove pre-existence against HEAD.

The 2026-10-24 tip gate failed in two more component tests with the same flake pattern. Adding them to the known-flake record keeps the next session from misreading them as regressions, while still requiring the isolated rerun.

The recorded vitest baseline predates the RLS-inclusive run, so a later session cannot tell whether a new count is a regression or a different suite. The 2026-10-25 tip-gate result gives the current reference.
Tip gate run in a detached worktree needs the test-rls lock so a peer session cannot run RLS tests against the same local stack at the same time; the lock must be cleared even when a step fails.
Targeted vitest run was wrapped in `timeout 170`; macOS zsh lacks that binary, so the gate silently never ran until re-issued without it. Durable pitfall for any gate run in this repo.

A green-looking vitest run silently skipped 51 RLS files. The gate skill's baseline lines are RLS-inclusive, so an unflagged run looks like a regression of 544 tests rather than a missing flag. Recording the flag prevents a false pass or a false alarm.

The 2026-10-31 email-switch session ran tsc/eslint/vitest/build on a merged tree while Docker was down. Its gate script first refused ("REFUSE: API_URL= not local"), then the agent injected placeholder keys to get a run. The skill does not say what to do when the stack is down, and does not cover gating a merge without moving a ref.
A tail-truncated gate hid the failing test names; the lesson is to rerun untruncated and reconcile counts before reporting a gate result.
A phase was presented as gated after only the affected suites were re-run following review fixes; the phase-completion protocol requires the full chain.

A handoff's gate count was stale: the live run gave 4 hits, not the claimed 3. The gate skill has baselines but no rule to re-run a handoff-quoted count and attribute each hit to the base commit before reporting it.

A next build run in a detached worktree with a symlinked node_modules failed with exit 1. Turbopack rejects a node_modules symlink that points outside the root. The skill says to clone with cp -Rc but does not name this failure, so the next run may symlink again and misread the result as a code failure.
The RLS suite failed in run 4 of 4, deadlocking with DDL-in-transaction files. The fix (a serial stage) and the RLS_RACE skipIf that hid a test are gate-running knowledge not in this skill.

The two-stage test:rls split is already recorded, but the episode showed the split was verified by listing files per stage, not by trusting the script edit. Add that check so a future split is proven, not assumed.

The skill already lists PublishDraftButton as a flake, but only for one test name. On 2026-11-01 a different test in the same file failed the first full run and passed isolated and on rerun. The flake is file-level, and the skill should say so. The recurrence across three handoffs with no fix card is the other half of the lesson.

The existing rule already requires RLS_TESTS=1, and it was missed on 2026-11-01. The run reported 1883 passed and 544 skipped, which is the unflagged signature, and it went into the handoff as a green tip gate. Adding the recurrence and the skip-count tell makes the miss easier to catch.
The orchestrator stopped its dev server before the gate chain because both share .next, but the skill only tells you to check for a dev server after tsc fails. Make the pre-chain stop explicit.

The 2026-11-03 RLS-inclusive vitest run failed one test with a database error, not a timeout. The flake rule names only timeouts, so a future session could treat a non-timeout RLS failure as a regression or round it up to a pass.
Pointer repair: time-dependent-test-fixed-clock is absorbed into the test-authoring umbrella this run.

A full vitest run failed two NewEventForm timeouts that passed 70/70 alone. This is a second instance of the per-file timeout flake the skill already documents; recording it under the same rule keeps the next run from reporting the total as green.
The gate wrapper's completion notice came early and nearly led the agent to a premature green claim. The stop condition must be the sentinel, not the notification.

On 2026-11-14 the full vitest run failed one serial-stage RLS file with a deadlock; the serial stage passed the same file. The static-gates skill names the serial stage but not how to classify a deadlock seen in the full run.

Full vitest gate was reported with a non-zero exit and unhandled teardown errors; the rule that a run must exit 0, plus the DEFERRED-row requirement, is missing from the gate skill and the flake rules only cover per-test failures.

Full vitest run on 2026-11-20 exported only API_URL from supabase status; the guard in tests/helpers/clients.ts refused 61 files and the run reported 62 failed files. The mapping existed only as prose in one bullet. Making the exact command and the failure signature explicit prevents the same misread and stops a config failure being reported as test failures.

Review dispatch on 2026-11-20 forbade heavy gates for reviewers, but the skill states the rule only for the main chain. Reviewer briefs need the same rule, plus the spot-check label for scoped vitest runs.
Fold the narrow gate-behaviour sweep into the static-gates umbrella as the 'after changing a gate' subsection; sibling deleted after this lands.

The episode reported a load flake correctly as a flake but left it unrecorded, so the next session would meet the same unknown failure with no history. The existing rule only covers DEFERRED rows for ReferenceError flakes; this extends the same discipline to all new flakes.

Bare `pnpm test:rls` ran against .env.local (Seoul) and the guard failed all 52 files. The skill's exact env command covers only vitest run. Load from concurrent review agents also caused timeouts that this skill's flake rule should name.

The r4 walk ran a bare `pnpm test:rls` that read .env.local (Seoul), and only the URL guard stopped it. The next two reruns failed because the env export was built with sed and came out empty. The skill already names the eval form, but it does not say sed is unsafe or that an empty API_URL must stop the run.
